canon.origin: Kirk's fictional generative lineage; the shared substrate establishes common origin, not interchangeable identity.
canon.principle: Twenty independent adult men emerge from one generative lineage. Their faces, proportions, temperaments, competencies, specializations, relationships, and growth paths remain distinct.
canon.continuity: Every man has a persistent identity and dated growth history. Later generations inherit selected traits and practices but never copy a predecessor wholesale.
canon.boundary: All twenty are fictional adults aged 24–41. Numeric dimensions are production baselines, not claims about real people. No real-person likeness is assigned.

production_standard.reference_sheet: One character per sheet: head front/three-quarter/profile/back; full-body front/side/back; four signature poses; neutral plus three readable expressions; hands/feet detail; silhouette and proportion callouts.
production_standard.camera: Orthographic or long-lens neutral reference camera; consistent eye height; full figure in frame; no wide-angle distortion; neutral grey studio; even key/fill/rim lighting.
production_standard.anatomy: Adult anatomy with stable landmarks, joint centers, limb lengths, muscle insertions, and natural asymmetry. No whole-body scaling as a substitute for regional growth.
production_standard.modularity: Head, hair, neck, torso, chest/back inserts, upper arms, forearms, hands, pelvis, thighs, calves, feet, wardrobe, footwear, accessories, and props remain separable.
production_standard.rig: Humanoid rig with clavicle/scapula, spine, pelvis, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee, ankle, hand, and foot controls; corrective shapes for high-flexion and high-load poses.
production_standard.materials: Separate skin, hair, cloth, rubber, leather, metal, and painted-equipment materials; preserve pore scale and roughness across renders.
production_standard.provenance: Every render records character_id, generation, asset_id, prompt version, model/tool, seed when available, date, and parent asset IDs.
